races.name: Racing Tv Club Day Novices' Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Porcupine Bank
runners_data.note: Rates a confident favourite on OR 130 and two recent wins on Good going; Sean Bowen and Gordon Elliott is a potent pairing, though the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] flag notes it is marginally out of natural role here — not a material concern in a two-horse field where it will simply take the lead unchallenged across 2m6f on Good to Firm.

runners_data.name: Fine Thing
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on Good and has a clean two-from-two record on similar going, making the surface no concern; Harry Skelton's record on this type is strong and the Skelton yard is firing (2/5 in 14 days), but Fine Thing faces a 10lb OR deficit against a horse that has beaten stronger fields recently.

races.paceDynamic: With only two runners, Porcupine Bank is the sole front-running force in this 2m6f novice hurdle at Stratford, and on Good to Firm ground will set a controlled, uncontested tempo from the outset. Fine Thing, also a prominent racer, will shadow Porcupine Bank throughout, meaning this effectively becomes a two-horse match run at whatever rhythm Porcupine Bank dictates. With no pressure from behind and no hold-up horses to mount a late challenge, the race shape is essentially a controlled procession that will be decided on class and jumping ability in the home straight. This strongly favours the horse with the highest cruising speed and best jumping under a sustainable gallop — a prominent racer who can quicken off a steady pace is the clear beneficiary, with Porcupine Bank's superior OR of 130 and recent winning form giving it the edge in that profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clear Away
scenarios.trigger: If Porcupine Bank dictates a sustainable gallop throughout and kicks clear from the final flight.
scenarios.body: Porcupine Bank controls tempo from the front, conserving energy over the 2m6f trip on fast ground, and simply outstays Fine Thing when the race quickens up late. The higher OR, Gordon Elliott's targeting (23 days fresh), and two recent wins on Good underpin this as the dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fine Thing Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If Fine Thing's 2m4f–2m6f Good ground form proves superior and Porcupine Bank's jumping under pressure wavers.
scenarios.body: Fine Thing, trained by Dan Skelton and ridden by Harry Skelton, has won over 2m4f on Good and will press Porcupine Bank closely, exploiting any jumping error or stamina fade on the testing trip. With a 100% Good-going win rate and a sharp Skelton yard in form (2/5 in 14 days), this scenario is plausible if Porcupine Bank finds the trip a yard too far.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If either horse makes a costly jumping error mid-race that forces a race reshaping.
scenarios.body: In a two-horse field, a significant jumping blunder by either runner could dramatically alter the complexion — the error-free rival simply inherits the lead and controls the race without further contest. This is a pure execution risk scenario rather than a tactical one, relevant given both runners are novice hurdlers still learning their trade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish, Dead Rubber
scenarios.trigger: If both horses track each other so closely that the race is only settled in the final strides.
scenarios.body: With two prominent runners tracking each other throughout, if neither can generate a meaningful kick, the race degenerates into a flat-out sprint from the last hurdle home. This scenario favours whichever horse has the sharper turn of foot on Good to Firm ground, but is unlikely given the class gap and Porcupine Bank's recent dominant winning form.

watchPoints.text: Watch Porcupine Bank's jumping at the early hurdles — as a 4-year-old novice setting its own pace on Good to Firm, any mistake in the first mile could let Fine Thing take a decisive lead with no other horse to cover the gap.
Monitor the early sectionals: if Porcupine Bank sets an unusually slow tempo, Fine Thing under Harry Skelton may elect to push on and steal the race on the front end, flipping the expected outcome.

With only two runners, market moves at the off carry outsized significance — any late drift on Porcupine Bank (currently OR favourite) in a two-horse race warrants attention as an indicator of fitness or going concerns flagged by the Elliott yard.

Fine Thing's 36-day absence is slightly longer than Porcupine Bank's 23 days; in a fast-ground novice over 2m6f, race-fitness could be a marginal but real factor if the pace quickens sharply from the third-last hurdle home.

races.name: Happy 70th Birthday Helen Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Notnowlinda
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton — a combination who squeeze maximum value from patient tactics — and her best form figures on good ground (9/15 similar-going runs showing a 0W4P profile) suggest she needs things to go her way; 105 days off is a flag worth noting, though Skelton runners often return fit.|

runners_data.name: Rebel Tribesman
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's five-year-old has a superb record of 2W5P across all five recent runs on good ground, all in a front-running role, and goes to post fresh on 33 days' rest with his trainer firing at 2/2 in the past 14 days; the uncontested lead here is a significant tactical gift.|

runners_data.name: Kom Tu Voudras
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's six-year-old has the tongue-tie fitted and arrives 27 days post-run with a win and a second among his five recent outings; by inclination a hold-up horse, he will be operating against his grain if he tries to race prominently, and that style-fit discount is a real consideration against a leader who will not be caught napping.|

runners_data.name: Torrent
runners_data.note: Equipped with a hood and placed three times from ten runs on good-equivalent going, this Nigel Hawke five-year-old is a consistent hold-up type who has never won on similar ground in five attempts; he will need Rebel Tribesman to come back to him, rather than him to bridge the gap under his own steam.|

runners_data.name: Kittys Glance
runners_data.note: Alan King's lightly-raced five-year-old has a tidy form string of 01-232 and a strong record of W1P5 on good, but she is a genuine closer by nature and, shown in midfield on the map only because there are more hold-up types than rear positions, she is not truly a prominent racer; Tom Bellamy will need to be creative if she is to overcome a race shape that suits the leader.|

races.paceDynamic: Rebel Tribesman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, he will dictate terms at whatever tempo suits Jonathan Burke from the front. On good-to-firm ground over 2m6f at Stratford — a tight, turning track that rewards jumping fluency and a prominent position — that uncontested lead is a meaningful tactical asset, particularly given Rebel Tribesman's consistent form figures of 122-12. The remainder of the field — Notnowlinda, Torrent, Kom Tu Voudras and Kittys Glance — are all hold-up or off-the-pace types, meaning they will be chasing a horse who has already banked a rhythm lead and faces no early pressure. This race shape strongly favours the horse able to control fractions from the front, with hold-up runners dependent on a collapse in the leader that may never materialise; the field holds more true hold-up types than the map can show at the rear, and Kom Tu Voudras and Kittys Glance — both genuine closers by nature — have been redistributed into midfield on the map, with Rebel Tribesman almost certain to secure the front position unchallenged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rebel Tribesman Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Tribesman jumps cleanly and bowls along at a sustainable gallop with no rival pressing him for the lead.
scenarios.body: He travels comfortably in front, controls the tempo, and arrives at the final flight with enough petrol to repel challengers; his form figures of 2-1-2-1 on similar going underline he is a genuine front-runner who finishes his races.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Close Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Tribesman sets a strong enough pace that he ties up inside the final half-mile, opening the door for hold-up horses to get into it.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-comfortable tempo would mean Rebel Tribesman's advantage is eroded approaching the last, allowing hold-up horses with fresh legs to close; Notnowlinda with Harry Skelton has the class and the going form to be the most dangerous finisher in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Sit-And-Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is modest and one of the shorter-priced hold-up types positions closer than usual, turning it into a sprint finish from the last.
scenarios.body: A slow, messy race would compress the field and make positional advantage less decisive, giving Kittys Glance or Kom Tu Voudras a chance to land a blow if they travel into a prominent spot; however, both are true hold-up types redistributed forward on the map and neither is naturally suited to this role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Grinds Field Down
scenarios.trigger: If the good-to-firm ground and the stamina demands of 2m6f produce errors and a strung-out field where only the most durable survive.
scenarios.body: A gruelling race of attrition would put the emphasis on jumping accuracy and staying power over raw speed; Torrent, equipped with a hood and placed twice at this trip on good ground, could emerge from the wreckage if the principals empty.

watchPoints.text: Rebel Tribesman's jumping is the single biggest variable — if he fires round cleanly and Jonathan Burke gets a rhythm lead from the off, the rest of the field may simply never get close enough to threaten.|

Notnowlinda returns after 105 days off and, while the Skelton operation is capable of presenting horses fit first time back, a race that unfolds at a modest pace in front of her could leave Harry Skelton with too much ground to make up at the finish.|

Kom Tu Voudras and Kittys Glance are both natural hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to the density of rear-runners in this small field; if neither can secure an improved position, they risk being caught in no-man's land — not close enough to the pace to challenge, not far enough back to produce a meaningful late run.|

The good-to-firm ground at Stratford rewards accurate jumping and a forward position around this tight track; any horse that makes a significant error at a hurdle will concede ground that is very difficult to recover on a surface this quick over 2m6f.|

races.name: Brian And Sheila Vaughan Memorial Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Crebilly
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill (1 win from 6 runs in 14 days), returning after 53 days off; placed twice on good ground at similar distances but must overcome his deep hold-up style in a small six-runner field where the pace is likely to be honest rather than explosive.

runners_data.name: Magistrato
runners_data.note: Excellent recent form with four wins from five on good ground at 20f, and James Bowen takes the ride for Deborah Cole (no runners in 14 days); 152 days since last run is the key query, but his prominent racing style is perfectly suited to sitting just off the contested early pace and he is the most consistent good-ground performer in the field.

runners_data.name: Bagheera Ginge
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with a superb good-ground record (14 from 15 sim-going runs) who will bid to dominate under Sam Twiston-Davies; trainer Nigel Twiston-Davies has been quiet (0 from 5 in 14 days), but Bagheera Ginge's three wins from five recent outings and the 'v' headgear flag suggest he is a headstrong type who needs to be first away — the contest with Sir Tivo for the lead is the defining tactical variable.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Consistent six-year-old with form figures of 112213 and four wins from 13 runs on good ground; Sean Quinlan rides for a trainer in form (3 from 8 in 14 days), and his prominent style means he will likely slot in just behind the duelling front-runners — the step up in trip from his recent 17f runs to 2m3½f is the one slight query to resolve.

runners_data.name: Parisencore
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse trained by Nicky Richards (2 from 4 in 14 days) returning after 39 days; a winner at 20f on good ground and placed on softer, but his hold-up style in a six-runner field with two confirmed front-runners means he needs a genuine pace collapse to get competitive in the straight.

runners_data.name: Sir Tivo
runners_data.note: Veteran 12-year-old front-runner who has won twice recently including a 17f handicap chase on good ground; Gary Hanmer (0 from 4 in 14 days) is quietly handled, but Sir Tivo's twin-track plate headgear and natural front-running style ensure he will dispute the lead with Bagheera Ginge — his stamina over this longer 2m3½f trip relative to his recent wins at 15-18f is the key concern if the duel is prolonged.

races.paceDynamic: Bagheera Ginge and Sir Tivo are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the off, creating a genuine pace battle over the first mile of this 2m3½f chase on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Bagheera Ginge has the stronger recent front-running form (three wins in his last five on good ground) and Sam Twiston-Davies will likely push to dominate, but Sir Tivo — a two-time recent winner who has also led — will not simply concede, meaning the pace is set to be honest to brisk rather than dawdling. With two genuine lead horses fighting for supremacy, the race shape strongly favours prominent-to-hold-up types who can sit just off a contested gallop, conserve energy over the fences, and pick up the pieces when the leaders' duel takes its toll in the closing stages. Prominent runners with strong stamina credentials and proven good-ground form — particularly Magistrato and Captain Cool — are best positioned, while the deeper hold-up horses carry more risk given the field of only six.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Bagheera Ginge and Sir Tivo fight for supremacy and set a genuine gallop that stretches the field from flagfall.
scenarios.body: The pace duel consumes both front-runners approaching the final circuit, leaving the race wide open for the prominent pair tracking just behind to pounce from two out; the honest gallop on good-to-firm ground rewards stamina and jumping precision over raw speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Tivo capitulates early and Bagheera Ginge is allowed to front-run unchallenged at a controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: Bagheera Ginge, uncontested and able to dictate a more measured gallop, conserves enough energy to jump fluently throughout and find extra when challenged from two out; his excellent good-ground record (three wins from five) and Twiston-Davies' tactical nous make this a credible alternative if Sir Tivo is outpaced early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to bring Crebilly and Parisencore into play from the back despite their wider draws off the pace.
scenarios.body: A truly scorching gallop from the duelling front-runners burns off the prominent pair, allowing the hold-up horses to close with sustained runs from the final fence; Crebilly's single win and place on good ground and Parisencore's 2019 win on similar conditions offer slim but real claims if conditions are extreme.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Upset, Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are ridden conservatively and a slow early gallop produces a bunch finish at the last fence.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race rewards the best jumper at the final fence rather than the best stayer, introducing chaos into what should be a stamina test; in this unlikely scenario, younger, sharper horses like Captain Cool (six-year-old, consistent form figures of 112213) and Sir Tivo benefit from their jumping speed.

watchPoints.text: Bagheera Ginge and Sir Tivo — watch the opening exchanges closely; if both jockeys commit fully to the lead from the start, the resulting pace duel could be severe enough to compromise both horses' finishing prospects and dramatically boost the chances of Magistrato and Captain Cool.

Magistrato — 152 days off the track is the single biggest risk factor in this race; if he shows any sign of rustiness at his fences in the early stages, his prominent style could become a liability rather than an asset.

Captain Cool — watch whether Sean Quinlan elects to track the front-runners closely or gives himself a length of daylight; at 2m3½f (longer than his recent wins), his positioning in the first mile will be critical to whether his stamina holds to the line.

Crebilly — Harry Cobden is a high-class jockey dropped into a modest handicap; if the pace is scorching and the field strings out, watch whether Cobden switches Crebilly to the inner to save ground and mount a late challenge from off the final fence.

Parisencore — in a field of only six, watch whether Danny McMenamin opts to sit closer than Parisencore's usual hold-up style would suggest; any move to ride more prominently in a small field would be a live tactical signal worth monitoring from the off.

races.name: Quinnbet Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Dunkerque
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has won four of his last five including back-to-back victories this term, all in Good or Good to Firm conditions, sitting prominently and wearing headgear (hg:p); Jennie Candlish's yard is firing at 3/8 in the last 14 days and Sean Quinlan partners a horse ideally mapped for the sole stalking slot in a three-runner field.

runners_data.name: Samuel Spade
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who must produce his effort from last of three against a pair that will already have built a potentially decisive buffer; his similar-going record of 2W from 15 is modest, Beau Morgan claims 5lb but faces a tactical puzzle, and his best run this season (1/23f/GOO) came when he had a bigger field to counter-surf through.

runners_data.name: Krak
runners_data.note: Front-runner who gets a completely uncontested lead courtesy of the small field; Harry Skelton will manage the fractions shrewdly for Dan Skelton's yard and his three recent runs in Good ground (3rd, 4th, 2nd) show he handles conditions, though he is 12lbs below Dunkerque on official ratings and has not yet won over fences.

races.paceDynamic: Krak is the sole confirmed front-runner in this three-horse field and will dictate terms from the outset at Stratford's right-handed track over 2m6½f, setting a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground with no rival likely to challenge for the lead. Dunkerque (style=P) will track Krak in second from an early stage, meaning the race resolves into a straightforward duel between these two from some way out, with Samuel Spade (style=H) forced to make up ground from the rear. With only three runners, no meaningful pace pressure exists — Krak controls tempo, Dunkerque gets the perfect stalking position, and Samuel Spade must produce a sustained finishing effort rather than a late sprint, which is a harder ask over a truly-run 2m6½f on a summer surface. This race shape strongly favours the prominent tracker (Dunkerque) who gets a free rail-to-rail berth just off a lone leader at a comfortable tempo, able to pounce without expending energy hunting a pace group that doesn't exist.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces On Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Krak sets a sustainable gallop and Dunkerque tracks throughout before asserting from two out.
scenarios.body: Dunkerque's position directly behind Krak at an uncontested pace is the most advantageous in a three-runner field, and his five wins from 15 similar-going starts, including back-to-back wins this term, confirm his ability to capitalise on exactly this setup. Krak, having set the fractions without a fight, may have enough left to hold on for a share of the prize, while Samuel Spade must pass both from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Krak dictates a genuinely slow tempo and conserves enough energy to repel Dunkerque's challenge on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Krak's trainer Dan Skelton has two winners from five runners in the last 14 days and Harry Skelton's judgement of pace means Krak could steal a march by presenting minimal gaps for Dunkerque to exploit late. Dunkerque's similar-going record makes him the main danger, but a slow-run race over fences can produce an advantage for the horse that travels widest and longest in front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Krak and Dunkerque burn each other out and Samuel Spade delivers one sustained burst to sweep them both up.
scenarios.body: Samuel Spade has won from hold-up tactics before (1/23f/GOO), but his form in similar going reads 8/15 with only two wins from fifteen and he needs the front pair to over-exert in a race that, by its nature, is likely to be unhurried.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses In Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a jumping error or exit changes the complexion dramatically, reducing the contest to a two-horse or even one-horse race.
scenarios.body: With only three runners over fences, a single incident — a fall, unseated rider, or a badly lost position after a blunder — could radically alter the order and hand the spoils to whichever runner survives cleanest.

watchPoints.text: Dunkerque's headgear (hg:p) has coincided with all five recent wins — if it continues to sharpen his focus travelling behind Krak, he is the most dangerous horse at any stage from the third-last fence onward.

Krak's jumping under Harry Skelton needs monitoring at the first few fences — a blunder at an early obstacle with only two rivals could see the field reorganise completely and undermine Skelton's pace-control plan.

Samuel Spade's hold-up style leaves him reliant on the front two tiring; if this race is run at a crawl, he may find himself three lengths off with nowhere near enough time to close, making his 160lbs weight burden even more costly.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed on course — all three horses show OK going flags, but Dunkerque's sim-going record of 12/15 including five wins gives him the strongest surface profile in the field.

With only three runners the market will be tight and short-priced; watch for any significant drifts or steams in the final 30 minutes that may reflect stable confidence, particularly from the Skelton operation whose trainer strike rate (T14:2/5) is notable.

races.name: Happy Birthday Sue Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Glenmalure Flyer
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's eight-year-old is a natural hold-up horse who arrives on a 51-day break wearing a hood, with solid good-ground credentials (1W2P in similar going) and form over distances beyond two miles suggesting this 3m3½f trip is within range; Harry Skelton takes the ride in what looks an ideal race shape for his style.|

runners_data.name: Winning Paddy
runners_data.note: Alexandra Dunn's consistent eight-year-old hold-up performer has been placed or won in five of six good-ground starts and won over 26f, making the trip and conditions credible; Richie McLernon steers and the trainer's 1/1 14-day strike rate is worth noting, though OR 92 means he concedes weight to the higher-rated Glenmalure Flyer.|

runners_data.name: Yes And Yes
runners_data.note: Belinda Clarke's nine-year-old has won twice in five good-ground starts and is genuinely a hold-up type at heart, but with two other confirmed back-markers in this small field, it is unlikely to settle at the very rear — racing closer to midfield than natural, the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag tempers confidence that it can reproduce its best form from an unnatural position, even though the form figures (1-1 recent wins) are eye-catching.|

runners_data.name: Illogical Logic
runners_data.note: Christian Williams' eight-year-old is a straightforward front-runner whose recent form string (346P-5) is modest, but its role here is pace-maker in chief over this marathon trip; Jack Tudor takes a solid booking, yet OR 81 and no wins in similar going across nine attempts limits confidence it can sustain the gallop it sets all the way to the line.|

runners_data.name: Flashy Boy
runners_data.note: Robbie Llewellyn's nine-year-old is another confirmed front-runner, returning just 32 days after its last run, but crucially has zero wins or places from nine good-ground starts — the going here is likely a genuine concern and its tendency to jump big-and-bold at pace may prove costly in a contested lead scenario over this extended trip.|

runners_data.name: The Kings Soldier
runners_data.note: A young five-year-old trained by Tracey Leeson, carrying top weight alongside Flashy Boy at 142lbs, who has been consistent without winning (0W2P in similar going) and brings genuine front-running intent; Oscar Palmer claims 7lbs which partially offsets the burden, but the inexperience of a five-year-old in a pace-war over 3m3½f is a significant stamina question.|

races.paceDynamic: Illogical Logic, Flashy Boy, and The Kings Soldier are all confirmed front-runners in a six-runner field, meaning an unrelenting gallop is virtually certain from the opening fence over 3m3½f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Three horses cannot all lead, so a fierce battle for supremacy will develop early, burning through each other's stamina reserves and setting up a truly severe test for those attempting to dominate from the front. The prolonged pace ensures that this race shape is built almost entirely in favour of hold-up horses with the class and stamina to finish powerfully from off a strong pace — Glenmalure Flyer and Winning Paddy are the natural beneficiaries. Yes And Yes is a genuine hold-up type whose true style cannot be accommodated at the rear given the volume of back-markers, so it has been mapped to midfield — that redistribution means the closers' scenario is carried by fewer genuinely natural hold-up horses than the map implies, and that weight falls most cleanly on Glenmalure Flyer and Winning Paddy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Illogical Logic, Flashy Boy, and The Kings Soldier fight a genuine three-way battle for the lead, burning stamina from the outset.
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop over this extreme distance on quick ground drains the front-runners long before the home straight, leaving the race entirely open to horses who have been able to conserve energy from off the pace. Glenmalure Flyer and Winning Paddy, both proven hold-up types at this sort of trip in good going, are optimally placed to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners establishes a clear lead early while the other two burn each other out fighting for second.
scenarios.body: Rather than three-abreast carnage, one pace-setter — most likely Illogical Logic given the better class — slips clear while the others neutralise each other, producing a controlled but still honest gallop that rewards the leader's jumping fluency and fitness. The hold-up horses still close but may find the leader too far ahead to reel in, and a prominent type who settles just off the lead could be best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners' early rivalry causes one or more to capitulate at halfway, dramatically collapsing the pace for the final circuit.
scenarios.body: A sudden slowdown mid-race would allow resting front-runners to recover briefly, complicating the closers' timing and potentially allowing a revived pace-setter or a horse tracking prominently to kick at a key moment. Yes And Yes, if having secured a forward position under the redistribution scenario, could be the horse most capable of exploiting a reshaped race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Clears the Field
scenarios.trigger: If the combination of extreme trip, fast ground, and relentless pace causes multiple fallers or pulled-up horses, turning it into a survival event.
scenarios.body: With three front-runners setting a fierce standard over 3m3½f on good-to-firm, attrition through jumping errors or fatigue becomes a real factor, and whoever is still jumping cleanly and travelling at the final fence takes the race almost by default. The Kings Soldier, young at five and consistent in recent form, could benefit from rivals' misfortune, as could the proven stayer Winning Paddy if the field thins dramatically.

watchPoints.text: Flashy Boy has zero wins or places from nine good-ground starts — if the ground officially rides faster than advertised on this card, Flashy Boy's ability to even complete the trip at the pace it sets is a serious query.

Three front-runners (Illogical Logic, Flashy Boy, The Kings Soldier) cannot all hold the lead — watch the first three fences for a brutal early speed battle that could cause a jumping error or early exit from one of them, reshaping the race entirely.

Yes And Yes is a proven hold-up horse forced into midfield by the race shape — if it fails to settle in an unnatural position early on, it risks using energy that is meant for the finish, undermining its strong recent winning form.

Glenmalure Flyer has not run for 51 days — Harry Skelton and Dan Skelton are adept at placing horses fresh, but watch the market move for any sign the stable believes an absence this length is a concern over such a demanding trip.

The Kings Soldier's jockey Oscar Palmer claims 7lbs but is only five years old as a horse — monitor its jumping accuracy as the race develops, as inexperience in a prolonged stamina test under a big pace may expose it late in the race.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Reteti
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare in consistent form with four placings from five on good ground over this trip; Marc Goldstein rides for the in-form Sheena West yard, and the 52-day break is not a concern given her fresh-horse record, but she needs a genuinely strong pace to deliver her late effort against a field that may not provide it.

runners_data.name: Eyeeye
runners_data.note: Brendan Powell partners this hold-up type whose recent form shows worrying fade patterns at the finish — flagged for late weakening — and a run finishing 17th on good ground over 12f suggests sharp-track pace at Stratford may not suit; consistent place-level form at this trip but the finishing kick concern is a real caveat.

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Jonathan Burke takes the ride for James Owen on this horse who has consistently placed at this trip and distance band; headgear note (p) suggests he needs to be organised early, and while his good-ground figures are acceptable (8 from 15 similar runs), he lacks a win from his recent attempts and may be vulnerable to more progressive rivals.

runners_data.name: Jet Patrol
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen, one of the strongest jump jockeys in the field, partners this nine-year-old for James Owen — a pairing that landed a win over this exact trip on good ground in the recent history; two wins from ten similar-going runs is a solid record, the headgear (t) suggests he is primed, and tracking a controlled pace suits his style perfectly.

runners_data.name: Diesel Line
runners_data.note: James Bowen rides this eight-year-old for the Pogson yard; his true racing style is hold-up from the rear but with multiple hold-up types in this field he will be compressed into a midfield berth that is not his natural home, reducing his effectiveness — the STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 reflects this positional squeeze and should temper expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Mayday Games
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner — Kielan Woods can simply slide to the front and set whatever tempo he chooses for Shaun Lycett; a recent Stratford win over this trip on good ground (going 1 from 7 on similar ground) is directly relevant, and uncontested lead makes him dangerous, though the class of closers behind him will test him from the third-last.

runners_data.name: Lord Cauvelliere
runners_data.note: Sean Houlihan's mount has placed in seven from seven starts on good going and won over 17f at this course type, making the step back to 2m½f workable for this prominent-style five-year-old; a 78-day absence is the one flag, but his consistent form profile and natural front-foot style means he will be in the firing line throughout.

runners_data.name: Clever Relation
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes over on this Christian Williams-trained six-year-old whose best form — a second on good ground over 16f — suggests ability when conditions align; his genuine style is hold-up from the back but the crowded rear means he is mapping to midfield, a position that is not his natural comfort zone, and only a small STYLE_FIT discount separates him from useful outsider territory.

runners_data.name: Berry Edge
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners Dan Skelton's eight-year-old who has five of his last five runs on soft ground — a significant flag on today's Good to Firm surface; he is a natural hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by the field's configuration, and the combination of going concerns (only 2 from 15 on similar conditions) and the positional compromise makes this a tough ask despite the quality of the Skelton operation.

runners_data.name: Glance At Me
runners_data.note: Shane Quinlan (3lb claimer) takes the ride on this Andrew Martin-trained eight-year-old who has been off the track for a staggering 793 days — by far the longest absence in the field; headgear (ht) suggests he has needed management, and while his last run form includes a win and a second on good ground, the layoff renders almost any assessment of current fitness speculative.

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: James Davies rides this Gary Hanmer-trained six-year-old who has the strongest going-matched profile in the race — 15 from 15 similar runs, a recent win, and four seconds in five starts on good ground at this trip; a natural prominent racer who will slot in close to Mayday Games and is ideally set up to pounce when the pace softens from the third-last.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: Nick Slatter (3lb claimer) partners this David Killahena & Graeme McPherson five-year-old on a workable each-way mark of OR 66; his instinct is to race from the rear but the hold-up congestion in this field forces him to midfield, a role he has not naturally filled, and the style penalty (STYLE_FIT 0.91) is a meaningful discount on a card that already favours more forward-travelling types.

races.paceDynamic: Mayday Games is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, Kielan Woods can dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground over 2m½f at Stratford. Lord Cauvelliere and Northern Rose will push forward from the prominent berths, ensuring the pace is respectable without becoming a war, and the race should unfold in a single-file, rhythm-driven manner that rewards horses travelling well through the race rather than those coming from far off the pace. The field nominally contains a cluster of hold-up horses — Diesel Line, Clever Relation, Berry Edge, and Angel Of My Dreams are all true come-from-behind types redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply no rear slot available in this configuration, meaning their natural style will be compressed and they are unlikely to find the clear passage a genuine hold-up run requires. The race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or tracking the pace comfortably — in a steadily-run but uncontested single-leader race on a fair surface, the prominent-to-midfield profile that can quicken from two out holds the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mayday Games Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Mayday Games leads unchallenged at a fair but unhurried tempo and the field strings out behind him.
scenarios.body: Kielan Woods settles Mayday Games into a rhythm from the front, the moderate pace suits those travelling well just off him, and as the race quickens from the third-last the prominent runners tracking him are best placed to pounce; Northern Rose and Lord Cauvelliere, both natural prominent types on going they handle, are ideally suited to close on a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Lord Cauvelliere or Northern Rose apply genuine pressure from the second-last and Mayday Games is found wanting late.
scenarios.body: The front-running pace proves just enough to stretch the hold-up horses but not enough to hold off the two prominent types who have been travelling within themselves; Northern Rose's strong recent form (four placings in five on good ground) and Lord Cauvelliere's consistent course-distance profile make them the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the leaders tire enough for a horse tracking mid-division to mow them down from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Jet Patrol, a course winner with strong good-ground credentials and the most experienced horse in the field over this trip, would be the prime candidate to pick up the pieces; Reteti's solid recent place record on good ground gives her each-way claims in this shape though her hold-up tag means she needs a strong gallop to bring her late run into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the straight and the true hold-up horses find a clean run from the rear.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because Diesel Line, Clever Relation, and Berry Edge are all redistributed out of their natural rear position and face a crowded midfield rather than the open ground a genuine late run demands; even if pace collapse occurs, their compressed starting position negates much of the tactical advantage they would ordinarily hold.

watchPoints.text: Northern Rose's good-ground form (15/15 in similar conditions, recent win) makes her the standout pace-shape beneficiary if Mayday Games sets an honest but manageable tempo — watch for James Davies to place her just off the leader's quarters from the outset.

Mayday Games is an uncontested front-runner who won at Stratford over this trip recently — if Kielan Woods controls the early pace and the field fails to apply pressure, a front-running steal is a live threat that the hold-up-heavy field is structurally poorly placed to counter.

Berry Edge's entire recent form base is on soft ground and today's Good to Firm surface is a significant step up in terms of firmness — despite Harry Skelton's claims, monitor the ground situation closely as conditions look quick enough to blunt his finishing effort.

Glance At Me has been off the track for 793 days; even with headgear applied and a sharp yard in theory, this degree of absence means fitness is genuinely unknown and the market should be treated with caution if she shortens on course.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Diesel Line, Clever Relation, Berry Edge, Angel Of My Dreams — will all be racing in unnatural midfield positions; watch the early stages to see if any attempt to drop back to their true style, as crowding through the body of the race could cause interference or positional chaos from the fourth-last hurdle onward.
